quote.exact: Radford's theorem now states that the Lyndon words are algebraically independent elements of this shuffle algebra, and generate it

note: Lean: for every field K of characteristic 0 and every linearly ordered type A, the algebra map from the polynomial ring on Lyndon words to the shuffle algebra, sending each variable to its word, is bijective (injective = algebraically independent, surjective = generate). The definitions are the archive's own and were read: ShuffleAlgebra K A is the free K-module on lists over A with the product given on words by the usual recursive shuffle (as a multiset of interleavings), and IsLyndon w says w is nonempty and lexicographically strictly smaller than each of its proper nonempty suffixes. The alphabet may be infinite. Proved in the same file as radfordShufflePolynomial_holds; used by the proof of riemannHypothesis (checked in the compiled dependency graph).
